drills.q: Write current-API Qiskit code to sample a Bell circuit at 1024 shots.
drills.a: qc = QuantumCircuit(2); qc.h(0); qc.cx(0,1); qc.measure_all(); counts = StatevectorSampler(default_shots=1024, seed=42).run([qc]).result()[0].data.meas.get_counts() ~ {'00': 512, '11': 512}.

drills.q: You see counts {'00': 497, '11': 527} for a Bell circuit. Broken?
drills.a: No: sigma = sqrt(0.5*0.5/1024) ~ 1.6%, so +-16 counts is one sigma; deviation of 30 total is normal shot noise. Only systematic imbalance (e.g., '01' appearing) indicates real error.
Circuits passed to Estimator must not contain measurements; it appends basis rotations internally per observable term. Strip measure_all()/measure() before submission.

drills.q: A 60-qubit Clifford-only QEC syndrome circuit crawls on the default simulator. Fix and quantify.
drills.a: Switch to stabiliser method: AerSimulator(method='stabilizer') or Stim. Stabiliser runs in polynomial time (O(n^2)-ish per gate), handling thousands of qubits vs ~45 cap for exact statevector.

drills.q: Your variational loop does one sampler.run() per parameter candidate. Restructure.
drills.a: Batch all candidates into ONE run call as multiple PUBs (or one PUB with a parameter sweep list) inside a Session; result[i] maps back to candidate i. Round-trip/queue latency dominates otherwise - batching cuts wall-clock several-fold.

drills.q: Simulator matches theory but FakeSherbrooke noisy sim already diverges. What changed?
drills.a: The fake backend injects calibration-derived noise: per-edge CX errors ~1e-3, readout error, T1/T2 decoherence. Divergence means your depth x error budget is exhausted; reduce 2Q count via optimization_level=3 or restructure layout.

drills.q: Why pin qiskit versions per project even for tutorials?
drills.a: Annual major releases carry breaking changes by design (18-month support). Unpinned code hits removals like 2.0's execute()/V1 primitives and fails with AttributeError instead of DeprecationWarning.

drills.q: Design a fair A/B of two backends for your circuit.
drills.a: Same logical circuit + seeds; transpile per backend at L3; record post-transpile 2Q count/depth and edge fidelities used; equal shots sized for smallest resolved probability; same mitigation level; >=3 sessions across days; compare with confidence intervals, prefer the backend whose worst day wins.

drills.q: When is resilience_level=0 the RIGHT choice despite available mitigation?
drills.a: Benchmarking raw hardware honestly, short-depth circuits where gate error sits below the statistical floor you care about, and cost-constrained screening runs - mitigation adds bias-reduction at 2-10x shot cost and contaminates machine-characterisation experiments.

drills.q: Porting Cirq->Qiskit, GHZ results come out reversed. Root cause and permanent fix?
drills.a: Endianness: Cirq measurement keys big-endian, Qiskit bitstrings little-endian. Fix: convert once at boundaries with explicit index mapping; validate with an asymmetric known-answer state since symmetric states (Bell) hide the bug.

drills.q: What failed when trying to pip install qiskit in a network-isolated sandbox, and why disclose that in a hands-on module rather than hide it?
drills.a: The install failed with a proxy/network connectivity error. Disclosing it and using a genuinely-run, cross-checked numpy statevector simulator instead of silently presenting untested Qiskit code as verified is the honest practice â€” labeling unrun code '# untested sketch' preserves trust in what actually was verified.

drills.q: A circuit works on a noiseless local simulator but transpiling it for real hardware inflates the gate count dramatically. What's the likely cause and fix?
drills.a: The real backend's coupling map doesn't support required two-qubit gates directly between the chosen qubits, forcing the router to insert SWAP gates (each ~3 CNOTs). Fix by checking backend.coupling_map before submission and choosing a logical-to-physical layout that keeps interacting qubits adjacent.
